latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The image preserved the materials and clock constraints but failed the exact counts for elephants and monkeys and did not make the elephants clearly playing with the monkeys. The elephant count score was extremely low, suggesting the six wooden elephants were not visually separable or not all depicted. The monkey count was also below threshold, likely due to overlap, merging, or missing monkeys. The interaction clause was too vague, so the verifier did not recognize a clear play relation between the elephants and monkeys.
expected_improvement: Six wooden elephants should be easier to count because the retry prompt requires two neat rows of three, with each elephant fully visible and separated.
Five plastic monkeys should be easier to count because the retry prompt requires a single row of five distinct monkeys, each fully visible.

The playing relation should be clearer because the retry prompt places the monkeys directly between the elephant rows and requires the elephants to face inward toward the monkeys with trunks reaching toward them in a shared play arrangement.
The already-passed two purple clocks constraint should remain satisfied because the retry prompt explicitly keeps exactly two purple clocks visible and separate from the animals.
preserve_constraints: Elephants must be present and visible.
Monkeys must be present and visible.
There must be exactly two clocks.
Clocks must be present and visible.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt stated exact counts and general visibility, but it did not impose a rigid, countable layout. It also described the animals as playing together without specifying an unambiguous visual interaction, so the generator could create a cluttered scene where objects merged or the relation was not apparent.
previous_plan_error.error_source: Prompt underspecified count layout and play interaction despite using quantity_counting and spatial_layout.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a structured, front-facing, countable composition: six wooden elephants in two rows of three, five plastic monkeys in one central row, and two purple clocks off to the sides. Make every animal complete, separated, and unobstructed. Define the play relation visually by having the elephants face the monkeys and reach toward them, so the elephants are clearly playing with the monkeys rather than merely coexisting.
regression_risks: Adding a structured layout could cause the generator to omit one elephant or one monkey, so the prompt repeats the exact counts and says no extras or duplicates.
The clocks could regress in count or color if attention shifts to animals, so the prompt explicitly preserves exactly two purple clocks.
The wooden and plastic material bindings could leak or be omitted, so the prompt binds wooden only to elephants and plastic only to monkeys.
repair_constraints: Show exactly six wooden elephants, no fewer and no more.
Make the six elephants visually separable, complete, unobstructed, and easy to count.
Show exactly five plastic monkeys, no fewer and no more.
Make the five monkeys visually separable, complete, unobstructed, and easy to count.
Make the elephants clearly playing with the monkeys by placing the five monkeys in the center and arranging all six elephants facing inward toward the monkeys with playful reaching poses.
Do not add extra elephants, extra monkeys, or extra clocks.

Arrange the five plastic monkeys in one clear central row between the elephant rows, each plastic monkey complete, separate, unobstructed, and easy to count. Make the elephants clearly playing with the monkeys: all six wooden elephants face inward toward the five plastic monkeys, with trunks reaching playfully toward the monkeys so the interaction is obvious. Place exactly two purple clocks in the background, one on each side, fully visible and separate from the animals. No extra elephants, no extra monkeys, no extra clocks, no duplicated or merged animals, no cropped objects.
